original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For the unsigned dirty connector of PR4231 over a ring of characteristic c, answer open question 1 of PR6035 (research/connector-five-halves-growth) for large c: generalize PR6035's lifted integer criterion to any base multiplicity u (valid for c>=u-1), give depth-two templates on six sources (u=9, every c>=8), seven sources (u=13, every c>=12) and eight sources (u=28, every c>=27), and conclude N(c)>=k*floor(c/2)+2*(c mod 2) with k=6,7,8 in those ranges via PR4248's concatenation and deletion lemmas.
scope_change_reason: Same scope change as PR6035: the PR4231 alphabet is kept and the source count grows, a scope-change trigger on the card. This answers the predecessor's recorded open question 1 directly (a six-source depth-two block valid for all large c).
bottleneck_link: Side result on the complete-call interface floor: it raises the batch size at which a characteristic-c connector consumer can pay exactly c calls per operator. No physical consumer, admission or transfer is supplied, so no kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop after uniform six-, seven- and eight-source depth-two templates with an all-large-c proof, direct block checks over a finite range of c and literal floor words for small cases. Report other searches only as local search notes.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json gives three base walks with per-source cuts. verify.py checks each integer two-prefix identity (63, 127 and 255 masks, the finite core of the proof), checks each expanded block directly modulo c and through the lifted readouts for u-1<=c<=64 (six and seven sources) and 27<=c<=40 (eight), simulates eight literal floor words (up to 196,764 calls) with generic coefficients, checks the corollary table against PR4248's counting condition for 8<=c<=128, and rejects nine mutation controls.

open_questions.question: Do six-source depth-two blocks exist for c=5,6,7, seven-source ones for 8<=c<=11, and eight-source ones for 12<=c<=26?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It fixes the best depth-two density at small characteristics, where the five-source bound of PR6035 still applies.
open_questions.first_step: Exhaust or SAT-encode the mod-c criterion at c=7 for six sources; local annealing reached 62 of 63 masks there.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only local annealing was run (best 52/63 at c=5, 58/63 at c=6, 62/63 at c=7; lifted u=8 also 62/63).

open_questions.question: Is there a depth-two block on k sources for every k once c is large enough?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Depth-two counting allows k up to about 2*log2(kc). A family with k ~ a*log c would give N(c) >= (a/2) c log c, matching the O(c log c) counting bound up to a constant and answering PR6035 open question 3 (N(c)/c unbounded).
open_questions.first_step: Run the lifted criterion for k=9 at larger base multiplicity, then look for an explicit recursive template (e.g. a product of two smaller lifted walks). Minimum characteristics found so far: 8, 12, 27 for k=6, 7, 8.
open_questions.blocked_by: Templates are found by search only; no general construction is known.

open_questions.question: Is there a depth-three block on more than 3k/2 sources, where k is the best depth-two block size at the same c?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only such a block would beat concatenated depth-two blocks; PR6035's 8/3 > 5/2 threshold is superseded by the 3, 7/2 and 4 densities here.
open_questions.first_step: Search lifted base walks under the integer three-prefix criterion at the base multiplicities used here.
open_questions.blocked_by: PR4248 reports a 125-of-127 search failure for seven sources at depth three in characteristic four only; no large-c depth-three search is recorded.

open_questions.question: Does any concrete consumer use a characteristic-c batch at a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The abstract call counts change no recursive supplier or kappa by themselves.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller with coefficients of characteristic c and price every primitive, admission and dispatch.
